examples.text: Спасибо, Гуля, мне очень приятно слышать.
examples.trans: Thank you, Gulya, I am very pleased to hear that.

examples.text: Спасибо вам огромное, шеф, можно вас обнять?
examples.trans: Thank you so much, Chef, may I hug you?

examples.text: Спасибо, папа!
examples.trans: Thanks, Dad!

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ятный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('pleasant').

examples.text: Спасибо, Гуля, мне очень приятно слышать.
examples.trans: Thank you, Gulya, I am very pleased to hear that.

examples.text: Приятного аппетита!
examples.trans: Enjoy your meal!

examples.text: Он очень приятный человек.
examples.trans: He's a very nice person.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hear', paired with 'услышать'.

examples.text: Вы слышали, наша хозяйка совсем умирает.
examples.trans: Have you heard, our owner is dying.

examples.text: Спасибо, Гуля, мне очень приятно слышать.
examples.trans: Thank you, Gulya, I am very pleased to hear that.

examples.text: Я ничего не слышал.
examples.trans: I didn't hear anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.text: Давай подождём, может, она улыбнётся ещё?
examples.trans: Let's wait, maybe she will smile again?

examples.text: Давай, Катя, побалуй своего хорошего парня.
examples.trans: Go on, Katya, spoil your nice guy a little.

examples.text: Давай вечером встретимся после смены.
examples.trans: Let's meet up this evening after the shift.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'баловать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'spoil / treat'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и побаловать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and spoil on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют побаловать.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to spoil.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.text: Давай, Катя, побалуй своего хорошего парня.
examples.trans: Go on, Katya, spoil your nice guy a little.

examples.text: Подумай хорошо, ты ведь такой молодой.
examples.trans: Think carefully, you are so young after all.

examples.text: Хорошо, теперь твой ход, пробуй.
examples.trans: Alright, now it is your move, taste it.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'boyfriend, guy, young man' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты мой парень?
examples.trans: Are you my boyfriend?

examples.text: Он хороший парень.
examples.trans: He is a good guy.

examples.text: Это друзья моего парня.
examples.trans: These are my boyfriend's friends.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'in the evening', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Давай вечером встретимся после смены.
examples.trans: Let's meet up this evening after the shift.

examples.text: Приезжай вечером.
examples.trans: Come in the evening.

examples.text: Вечером я дома.
examples.trans: I'm at home in the evening.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'третиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will meet', paired with 'встречаться'.

examples.text: Может, встретимся сейчас?
examples.trans: Maybe we could meet now?

examples.text: Встретимся в кафе.
examples.trans: Let's meet in the café.

examples.text: Аркаша, губернатор хочет с нами встретиться!
examples.trans: Arkasha, the governor wants to meet with us!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'after', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ладно, дочка, после об этом поговорим.
examples.trans: Alright, daughter, we will talk about that later.

examples.text: Ладно, после об этом поговорим.
examples.trans: Alright, we will talk about it later.

examples.text: Давай вечером встретимся после смены.
examples.trans: Let's meet up this evening after the shift.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мена'). Common feminine noun meaning 'shift (at school or work)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Огузок, почему ты снова опаздываешь на смену?
examples.trans: Oguzok, why are you late for your shift again?

examples.text: Давай вечером встретимся после смены.
examples.trans: Let's meet up this evening after the shift.

examples.text: Ну, давай, смелее пробуй своё блюдо.
examples.trans: Well, go on, taste your dish boldly.
